# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-4 (Extended v66)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse); 1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages); October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port after heavy weather, for repairs); **November 17, 1823 (convict Jean Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras, drowned, body not found, presumed entangled in Arsenal piles; newspaper account published)**; **December 24, 1823 (Christmas Eve, Montfermeil tavern scene, men drinking and smoking; Cosette sent for water; evening descends into full night); December 24-25, 1823 (afternoon: man in yellow coat searches Paris Boulevard de l'Hôpital; observed and pursued by police; boards coach for Lagny at half-past four; darkness falls; man exits at Chelles, proceeds to Montfermeil; encounters Cosette in forest carrying water bucket; brings her back to Thénardier hostelry; mysterious man seated at table; Cosette under kitchen table with knitting)**.

## Current Narrative Moment
**Evening at Thénardier Hostelry, Christmas Day 1823**: Mysterious man (yellow coat) seated at table; carters and peddlers drinking, three-quarters intoxicated, singing obscene refrain invoking Virgin and infant Jesus; Thénardier laughing with them; Madame Thénardier whispering to husband, counting money; Éponine and Azelma (Thénardiers' daughters) playing with cat; Cosette under kitchen table. Mysterious man produces doll and offers it to Cosette saying "It is for you"; Cosette initially retreats in terror, then gazes at doll with overwhelming emotion (described as feeling like being told "you are the Queen of France"), tears streaming, unable to take it, hides at extreme end under table. Tavern-keeper's face shows bestial acquisitive instinct; he scents the man as potential money-source; consults with wife in low voice.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; small village in 1823 with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier earning eight sous daily; toy-shop opposite Thénardier hostelry; Boulanger Lane); Dunstead (harbor town in England; Dungate nearby); Ravenmere; Staveford; Ostcombe; Kelford; Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby); Paris (Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, blind alley of La Planchette, Plat d'Etain coach office); Mediterranean; Balearic Isles; Nanterre; Suresnes; Switzerland; Pyrenees.

## The Mysterious Man in Yellow Coat
**Identity and Appearance**: Man in yellow coat; threadbare frock-coat; battered hat; walked Paris Boulevard de l'Hôpital seeking lodgings at modest houses; appeared foreign to Paris and quarter; observed by M. le Duc de Havré (captain of guard) during king's passage in royal carriage at two o'clock Christmas afternoon; drew notice of royal police; one agent ordered to follow; man eluded agent by plunging into deserted streets of faubourg as twilight fell; agent lost trace; report made to M. le Comte d'Anglès, Minister of State, Prefect of Police. **Exceptional strength noted**: grasped Cosette's water bucket with single hand; walked tolerably fast carrying bundle and cudgel; laid both on bench at hostelry with ease.

**Movements Christmas Afternoon/Evening**: After evading police agent, redoubled pace, frequently turned to assure himself not followed; at quarter-past four (night fully come) passed theatre of the Porte Saint-Martin where _The Two Convicts_ was being played; poster struck him; halted to read it; entered blind alley of La Planchette; entered _Plat d'Etain_ where coach office for Lagny situated; coach set out half-past four; man boarded, paid fare to Lagny, intended destination Chelles only; coachman observed he belonged nowhere, had no apparent means, did not enter inn, disappeared like he "dived through the earth."

**Journey and Forest Search**: Traveled with great strides through dark down principal street of Chelles; turned right before church into crossroad leading to Montfermeil; walked like person acquainted with country, had been there before; followed road rapidly; at intersection with ancient tree-bordered road from Gagny to Lagny, heard people coming; concealed himself in ditch until passers-by at distance; once in forest slackened pace, began careful examination of all trees advancing step by step as if seeking mysterious road known to himself alone; appeared to lose himself, paused in indecision; at last arrived by feeling way inch by inch at clearing with great heap of whitish stones; stepped up briskly, examined stones attentively through mists; large tree covered with vegetation warts nearby; went to tree, passed hand over bark counting warts as if seeking to recognize.

**Encounter with Cosette and Return**: While walking through thicket toward Montfermeil espied tiny shadow moving with groan, depositing burden, taking it up; drew near, perceived very young child laden with enormous bucket of water; approached child, silently grasped bucket handle; walked tolerably fast; Cosette followed without difficulty, no longer felt fatigue; raised eyes toward man with tranquillity and indescribable confidence; entered hostelry; laid bundle and cudgel on bench, seated at table; **Later produced doll and offered it to Cosette**; Tavern-keeper scents acquisitive potential in man.

## Cosette's Condition and Suffering (Winter 1823)
**Physical and Mental State**: Age 8; serving as servant to Thénardiers at Montfermeil; barefooted in winter; wore rags; bare feet thrust in wooden shoes; eye black from blow of Madame Thénardier's fist; weak but did coarse work; thin arms; wet and tiny hands. **Fear now habitual**: Fear diffused all over her; covered with it; drew elbows close to hips, withdrew heels under petticoat, made her occupy minimal space; allowed only absolutely necessary breath; became habit of her body admitting no variation except increase; in depths of eyes astonished nook where terror lurked.

**Labor**: Subjected to double pressure of man and woman; overwhelmed with blows (woman's); barefoot in winter (man's); ran upstairs and down, washed, swept, rubbed, dusted, ran, fluttered, panted, moved heavy articles; no mercy; fierce mistress and venomous master.

**Water Crisis and Night Errand (Christmas Eve)**: Thénardier hostelry drank little water; woman turned faucet; thin stream trickled, half-filled glass; declared "there is no more water!"; sent for water from spring despite darkness and terror; descended Boulanger Lane past lighted stalls; encountered woman who called her "the Lark"; continued into darkness; chose to flee through village and enter forest at run in desperation. **Spring journey**: Seven or eight minutes' walk from village edge to spring; guided by instinct; felt in dark for young oak leaning over spring; found branch, clung, bent down, plunged bucket; in violent excitement, strength trebled; while bent over, fifteen-sou piece fell silently into water from apron pocket (neither saw nor heard it fall); drew out bucket nearly full.

**Return in darkness**: Stared at great ruddy star near horizon traversing dense mist—unfamiliar, terrified her; planet resembled luminous wound; seized by black enormity of nature; something more terrible than terror; shivered with strangeness chilling to heart; eye grew wild; thought she should not refrain from returning at same hour morrow; began counting one through ten to escape singular state; hands wet felt cold; rose; terror unconquerable returned; one thought—flee at full speed through forest, across fields to houses; yet dared not without bucket due to Thénardier's fright-inducing power; seized handle with both hands; could hardly lift; advanced dozen paces, bucket full and heavy; forced to set down, breathe, resume march; walked bent forward with drooping head like old woman; weight strained and stiffened thin arms; iron handle completed benumbing and freezing of wet tiny hands; forced to halt; cold water splashing fell on bare legs; proceeded alone in depths of forest at night in winter far from all human sight—no one but God witnessed. **Lost coin in spring**: Fifteen-sou piece fell from her apron pocket while drawing water; neither saw nor heard it; loss unknown to her.

**Current Status at Hostelry**: Following mysterious man back without difficulty; now seated under kitchen table with knitting. After mysterious man offered doll, **Cosette began to rock swaddled sword (inadequate substitute for doll), singing in low voice "My mother is dead! my mother is dead! my mother is dead!"** Observed that no one watched her; crept out on hands and knees; seized doll in instant, returned to place under table casting shadow upon it to hide it from view. **Doll produces overwhelming emotion**: rare happiness of playing with doll contained all violence of voluptuousness. Then took doll, laid it gently on floor with veneration mingled with despair; without taking eyes from it, clasped hands, wrung them (unprecedented for her); wept, burst out sobbing—neither trip to forest, nor weight of bucket, nor loss of money, nor sight of whip, nor sad words from Madame Thénardier had wrung tears from her before. When man approached with doll, gazed at him as at sun; stared at doll; slowly retreated, hid herself at extreme end under table in corner of wall; face flooded with tears, eyes began to fill like sky at daybreak with strange beams of joy; felt moment comparable to being told "Little one, you are the Queen of France."

## Thénardier Family
**Male Thénardier**: Composite rascal of uncertain origin—probably Fleming from Lille in Flanders; exaggerated Waterloo prowess; ebb and flow, wandering, adventure characterized existence; tattered conscience entails fragmentary life; belonged to marauding sutlers of June 18, 1815 epoch. Peculiar rectilinear gestures; fine talker; appeared educated with improper pronunciation; cunning, greedy, slothful, clever; rarely wrathful but when enraged, terrible—bore deep furnace of hatred within; attentive and penetrating; highly intelligent; had look of sailors; "a statesman"; possessed certain cold tranquil laugh, particularly dangerous. Single thought: enrichment; lacked theatre worthy of talent; ruining himself at Montfermeil. Understood hospitality as merchandise; admirable poacher. Articulated aphorisms: duty to sell stews, repose, light, fire, dirty sheets, servant, lice, smile; stop passers-by, empty small purses, honestly lighten heavy ones; shelter families respectfully; shave man, pluck woman, pick child clean; know shadow uses up mirror; make traveller pay for everything. **Current behavior**: Cast second glance at mysterious man's threadbare coat and battered hat with husband; consulted husband with imperceptible forefinger movement and lip inflation signifying "a regular beggar"; went off to join drinkers' shouts of laughter; whispering to wife, counting money; **showed bestial acquisitive instinct upon sight of doll—stared alternately at doll and traveller, scenting the man as he would a bag of money; stepped up to wife and said to her in low voice** (text continues).

**Female Thénardier**: Formidable creature; loved no one except her children; feared no one except her husband. Mammiferous motherhood; maternity stopped short with daughters; did not extend to boys. Jealous of husband; deemed thin, yellow man must be coveted by all; dispensed with servants. Capable of wrath equal to husband's but his rarer; raised cover of stew-pan; seized glass; approached cistern deliberately; hideous, hyena mouth; wrath flashing in eyes; inspires terror in Cosette. Expressed disdain for threadbare coat and battered hat. **Currently whispering to husband, counting money over some sum**.

**Éponine and Azelma**: Two pretty little girls, more bourgeois than peasant in looks, very charming; one with shining chestnut tresses, other with long black braids hanging down back; both vivacious, neat, plump, rosy, healthy; warmly clad with maternal art; springtime not wholly effaced; light emanated from both; on the throne in toilettes, gayety, noise they made—sovereignty. When entered, Thénardier said to them in grumbling tone full of adoration, "Ah! there you are, you children!" **Playing with cat**: just executed important operation—got hold of cat; threw doll on ground; Éponine (elder) swathing little cat in spite of mewing and contortions in quantity of clothes and red and blue scraps; while performing this work saying to sister in sweet adorable language of children: "You see, sister, this doll is more amusing than the other. She twists, she cries, she is warm. See, sister, let us play with her. She shall be my little girl. I will be a lady. I will come to see you, and you shall look at her. Gradually, you will perceive her whiskers, and that will surprise you. And then you will see her ears, and then you will see her tail and it will amaze you. And you will say to me, 'Ah! Mon Dieu!' and I will say to you: 'Yes, Madame, it is my little girl. Little girls are made like that just at present.'"

## Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere Community
- **Pewyn**: counted coins twice, penny short; gave Nylia Corrford solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford
- **Yewyn Corrford**: appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; **married Tatho Brackick at Ravenmere before spring was out** (1824)
- **Ulrald Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Lura Haskick solemn promise to pay old debt owed to Stenson family
- **Nylia Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Pewyn solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford; read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints; laughed at story nobody else found funny; fell asleep in chair before fire caught; hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; only shrugged at question about rain
- **Yera Haskick**: gave Yewyn Corrford solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Dungate; late one night confided to Kassa Brackick that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after flood (CLAIM)
- **Lura Haskick**: recipient of Ulrald's debt-payment promise; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; shrugged about rain; asked "Will it rain, do you think?"; **apprenticed anew and became a cooper**
- **Kassa Brackick**: told Yewyn "price of salt is scandal"; received Yera's confidence about mill ledger
- **Elra Corrford**: sorted old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; walked long way round to avoid muddy square
- **Marald Corrford**: asked about rain; confirmed looking tired; **bought ribbon at stall and then regretted it**
- **Tatho Brackick**: rode out of Kelford; **married Yewyn Corrford at Ravenmere before spring was out** (1824); couple lived in Ravenmere
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there, did not return; CLAIM: Luena followed him to Staveford within the month
- **Rovus and Wenelle Lindmere**: wed at Ostcombe with half parish looking on; couple lived in Ostcombe
- **Fenelle**: laughed at story nobody else found funny
- **Isric Thornmere**: asked Vesmira if it will rain; Vesmira only shrugged
- **Jotho and Gadrek** (Ostcombe): agreed price of salt is scandal

## Main Characters Status
- **Jean Valjean**: Dead (drowned November 17, 1823, at Toulon)
- **Fantine**: Dead (buried in pauper's grave, January 1823)
- **Cosette**: Age 8; under Thénardier servitude; received doll from mysterious man; overwhelmed with emotion; hiding under table
- **Mysterious Man**: Arrived Christmas afternoon Paris; eluded police; boarded Lagny coach; disembarked Chelles; traveled to Montfermeil; encountered and aided Cosette; seated at Thénardier hostelry; produced doll for Cosette; acquiring-interest from Tavern-keeper
- **Napoleon Bonaparte**: Defeated, imprisoned at Saint Helena

## Themes
- Providence and divine intervention; human resilience against oppression
- Waterloo as historical hinge; war's moral paradox
- Mundane life indifferent to empires; daily tasks continue beneath grand narratives (Dunstead scenes interspersed with Montfermeil action)
- Mystery/obscurity: Mysterious man's identity, origin, purpose, forest search, doll acquisition
- Hidden transgressions and buried truths; lost coin in spring (unknown to Cosette)
- Human courage and compassion in extremis: child enduring suffering; mysterious stranger's silent aid and gift
- Poverty and exploitation; parasitic commerce of suffering; Thénardier's acquisitive instinct
- Terror and transcendence: child's dark night transformed by appearance of helper; doll as redemptive object; rare happiness bursting into tears
- Feminine childhood's imperative: doll as continuation of woman's future; Éponine's play contrasted with Cosette's deprivation
- Immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought
